title: Live-edit offset reconciliation for streaming metering (collaborative patch edits)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: We observed ambiguous and sometimes double billing when a client performs live edits (insert/delete/replace) to the active prompt/attachments during an ongoing streaming response. These collaborative patch operations shift token offsets, can trigger server-side re-tokenization, and interact badly with existing session snapshotting and ledger anchoring. The result is: (a) duplicate token debits for overlapping spans, (b) orphaned provisional credits that are never finalized, or (c) missed credits when the server treats a patch as a new request without reconciling prior emitted output.
reproduction_steps: 1) Open a streaming chat session and send an initial prompt containing a 3-paragraph context (client A).
2) Server begins streaming output tokens (server is on hosted cluster with KV-cache warmup).
3) While streaming, client B issues a patch: delete paragraph 2 and insert a revised paragraph at offset N. Patch uses collaborative OT-style transform (patch id + base offset).
4) Client retries the patch due to a transient 503 and the server receives it twice with different request IDs but same patch content.
5) Server performs on-the-fly re-tokenization and emits new tokens (some identical to previously sent tokens; some shifted).
6) Inspect billing ledger and per-session token tallies: observe duplicate debits for overlapping tokens and a provisional credit left open for the retried patch.
investigation_notes: - Logs show that streaming ledger anchors are tied to 'session_snapshot_id' created at stream start. Patches currently create a new ephemeral 'patch_snapshot' but the ledger finalizer treats any later snapshot as an independent billable request unless a special rollback executes.
- KV cache warmup path records tokens by absolute offset; when offsets shift the cache 'prefix' heuristics misattribute cache hits to the wrong ledger entry.
- Retry paths: duplicate patch delivery creates two separate provisional ledgers because dedupe keys are per-request and patches were translated to distinct request IDs by the proxy layer.

- Edge-case with attachments: when attachments change length, our tokenizer length estimation diverges from runtime tokenizer, causing final token counts to differ from provisional counts used for quota enforcement.
- Customer-reported incident (INC-2025-06) correlated to a collaborative editor integration; one customer saw 2-5x expected token charges during heavy live edits.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce 'edit-anchored snapshots' (EAS): on first stream start create EAS ID and bind all subsequent patches with a patch-sequence number rather than creating independent snapshots. This preserves a single billing anchor per user session.

2) Implement an idempotent patch ingestion layer with a globally unique dedupe key (client-provided patch-id + session EAS). If a duplicate patch arrives, recognize it and short-circuit ledger duplication.

3) Move to delta-crediting: credit/debit changes at patch granularity. When a patch deletes tokens already billed, create an explicit negative adjustment that finalizer can reconcile rather than trying to retroactively rewrite prior ledgers.
4) Improve KV-cache attribution: store cache hits against (EAS, patch-seq) instead of absolute offsets so warmup/match attribution remains correct even when offsets shift.

5) Tighten attachment length estimation: perform a server-side pre-tokenize pass at patch acceptance time to align provisional counts with final tokenizer output used in runtime. Record both provisional and final counts for auditability.

6) Create a reconciliation job that scans sessions with patches and ensures ledger invariants (no duplicate final debits for overlapping token spans). The job should emit alerts and attempt automated corrections for simple cases.
7) Backfill customer-facing docs and SDKs to explain that live edits are chargeable operations but that we will ensure no double-charging and provide credits when deletions reduce billed content.
qa_plan: - Unit tests for dedupe key generation and idempotent ingestion.
- Property-based tests that apply random sequences of insert/delete/replace patches and assert ledger invariants (sum of deltas == final billed tokens).
- Integration test harness that replays recorded customer session from INC-2025-06 and asserts corrected charges after reconciliation job runs.
- Performance test under high patch frequency to verify ledger finalizer latency stays within SLOs.
- Manual exploratory: create a 3-client collaborative session and intentionally trigger retries/partition events to verify no double-billing.
rollout_plan: - Feature-flagged rollout: enable EAS + dedupe in canary region with telemetry ON.
- Run reconciliation job in dry-run for 48 hours and surface diffs to billing audit dashboard.
- If diffs are <0.1% of total daily bill in canary, flip auto-correction on and expand to remaining regions over 7 days.
- Communicate to affected customers via in-console banner and support tickets when auto-corrections are applied.
- Post-rollout: monitor 'duplicate-debit' alert rate and reconciliation corrections weekly for 3 weeks.
acceptance_criteria: - No observed duplicate final debits for sessions with live edits across a 72-hour canary period.
- Reconciliation job successfully auto-corrects simple duplicates in canary (sampled), and audit trail shows coherent adjustments.
- Token counts reported in Console per-session match billing ledger within +/-1 token for 99.9% of sessions with edits.
- New metrics: 'patch-dedupe-hit-rate' > 99%, 'delta-credit-corrections' < 0.05% of daily bill after rollout.
comments: 2025-08-13 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial triage. Reproduced locally with editor simulator. Filing as P1 because customer saw billing shock. Attaching logs to Confluence.

2025-08-18 - Priya Raman (PM): Reviewed proposed EAS approach. Concern: behavioral change for downstream telemetry consumers that index by snapshot_id. Recommendation: emit mapping table snapshot_id->EAS to avoid breaking dashboards.
2025-08-21 - Marco Liu (Design): UX note: Console should show 'Live edit adjustments' line item in per-session cost breakdown when delta-crediting occurs. Will provide mockups by 2025-08-28.
2025-08-25 - Liam Chen: Implementation notes: started dedupe layer; found that gateway currently strips client patch-id. Need gateway change (dependency ENG-512000).

2025-08-30 - Security review request: no PII change expected but attachment pre-tokenize touches blob metadata. Confirmed no plaintext leak; we will only compute token counts from attachments using ephemeral worker. Security sign-off pending.
2025-09-01 - Aisha Kapoor: Recon job prototype passes dry-run on sample dataset (1000 sessions). Filing follow-up ENG-903211 for reconciliation heuristics tuning.
